author: United States Navy
title: Service record of John Charles Tashner Jr., October 1938 – January 1952
notes:
The record grew. In August 2026 this entry held two duty entries — Betio and Majuro — supplied by Jay Tashner's grandson as text. Later the same month the family supplied a transcription of the full service-record sheet: fourteen duty assignments with dates, rates and remarks from the Naval Training Station at Norfolk in October 1938 to VS-22 in July 1951, a list of Navy schools running to January 1952, officer correspondence courses, USAFI tests, and eight medals and commendations. Everything double-quoted below is the transcription's wording, its own spellings kept.

The spine of the career, as the sheet gives it: USNTS Norfolk (10/1938–02/1939, "In training."); USS Nitro (AE-2) deck force; USS Selfridge (DD-357), 04/1939–07/1941, "Deck force - radio striker - underwater sound operator - radio watches"; VP-23 at Pearl Harbor, 07/1941–11/1941, "Qualified for aviation in PBY aircraft"; Commander Patrol Wing TWO at Pearl Harbor, 11/1941–05/1942, RM3 then RM2, "Maintained watch of outlying islands and aircraft circuits - supervisor radio watch"; USS Ballard, written "USS BALLARD (AVP)", 05/1942–07/1942, "Standing radio watches during battle of Midway and search of battle area" and "Participated in capture of 36 Japanese officers and men from sunken Japanese Carrier"; CFAW-2 staff communications; FAW-14 at NAS San Diego, 11/1942–10/1943, PBY and PB2Y-3 radio instructor in flight, PB4Y-2 radio in flight, "Designated CAC."; CASU-16, 10/1943–05/1944, "Made invasion landing on Tarawa - Serviced PB4Y-2 and Army B-24 aircraft - Emergency repair - in charge of maintenance crew detachment on island of Betio"; CASU-30, 05/1944–04/1945, "Chief radioman in charge of electronics division fleet plane pool at Majuro, G1."; then the postwar run through radio material school, NAS Alameda, NAS Norfolk, VA-2E, VC-22 and FAETULant to VS-22, flying TBM-3S and TBM-3W aircraft as operator-technician with a secondary NJC of 9904, AEW/ASW operator technician. The medals list: Combat Aircrew Wings with Two Stars, American Defense Medal with Fleet Clasp, Good Conduct Medal with second and third award, Asiatic Pacific Ribbon with three stars, American Area Campaign Ribbon (the transcription spells it "Amewrican"), the World War II Victory Medal, and two commendations, June and August 1944, each "issued by Commander Marshall, Gilbert Area".

**The provenance is thin and that is still part of the citation.** This project has seen text and never paper: no scan, no photograph, no NARA or National Personnel Records Center reference. The transcription's misspellings — "Conmunications", "orerated", "eharge", "Amewrican" — look like an optical scan or a hand copy of a typed sheet, which is evidence that a paper exists and not a sight of it. Filing at `primary` remains a judgement about form (docs/sources.md rule 2), not a verification.

**The two transcriptions differ, and both readings are carried.** The duty-entry text supplied first reads "Serviced PBY and Army B24 Aircraft"; the full sheet reads "Serviced PB4Y-2 and Army B-24 aircraft". A PBY is a flying boat and a PB4Y-2 a land-based patrol bomber, so the difference is a real one. The sheet's reading sits beside a Consolidated-Vultee PB4Y-2 radio school in August 1943 and PB4Y-2 radio duties at FAW-14, which is circumstantial weight and not proof. Likewise "Majuro, G1." against the earlier "Majuro, G.I." — Majuro is in the Marshalls either way, and this project still edits neither.

Three cautions on the Ballard entry. The sheet writes her "(AVP)" where the reference designation for the converted Clemson-class destroyer is AVD-10 — filed as an abbreviation of the clerk's, quoted as given. The sheet says thirty-six Japanese officers and men where the general reference account of Ballard's one famous rescue says thirty-five; this project resolves neither number. And the sheet does not name the sunken carrier. The family's own research points at Hiryū, and the obvious archival follow-up is Ballard's war diary for June 1942 — a thread for the Midway pack (sand-lry.6), the way Betio leaves one for Tarawa (sand-lry.8).

What the record is good for now: the whole shape of a career, deck force to airborne early warning; that he transferred out of Selfridge and into naval aviation in July 1941, months before the attack; that on 7 December 1941 his billet was Patrol Wing TWO's communications at Pearl Harbor; that he was aboard Ballard for Midway and the search of the battle area; that the record itself, and not a family inference, says "Made invasion landing on Tarawa" — a sentence the two duty entries first supplied did not contain; the commendations, the schools and the medals. What it is still not good for: any hour of any morning, any date inside a range except where one is written, and the name of the carrier.
